title: Adaptive Latency Smoothing Engine for Geo-routing and Tiered Variant Escalation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Overview:
We need a robust scoring and decision layer for selecting geographic POPs (regions) and tiered capacity that smooths noisy latency telemetry while incorporating network path health signals. The goal is to avoid flip-flopping between POPs during short spikes, bias routing toward lower-cost variants when appropriate, and enable safe, automated fallback to alternative model variants when region/tier health degrades.

Goals:
- Produce a single composite score per POP per route that reflects short-tail and long-tail latency (p50/p95), packet loss/jitter signals, and tier preference penalties.
- Use smoothing windows to avoid reacting to short-lived anomalies while still detecting sustained regressions within minutes.
- Surface transparent thresholds and hysteresis so Console shows why decisions were made.
- Support a tier-weighted routing policy where enterprise/dedicated tiers are preferred unless health drops below SLA thresholds.
- Provide a variant escrow/warmup mechanism for graceful fallback to smaller/quantized models with automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Proposed scoring approach (high-level):
1) Telemetry preprocessing: ingest p50 and p95 per POP per route sampled at 10s resolution. Apply outlier filtering (median absolute deviation) and ignore samples with <50 requests in window.
2) Dual-window smoothing: maintain two EWMA windows per quantile — short (60s, alpha ~0.3) and long (900s, alpha ~0.03). Short EWMA catches sudden shifts; long EWMA captures steady drift.
3) Normalize quantiles to baseline for route/POP (baseline computed from rolling 7d median at similar hour-of-day) -> normalized_p50, normalized_p95 in [0.0, 1.0+] where 1.0 == baseline.
4) Network health penalty: compute net_health_score in [0,100] combining packet loss, TCP retransmit rate, and regional BGP anomalies. Map to penalty factor between 0 and 1 (1 => healthy, 0 => unhealthy).
5) Tier weight and cost bias: apply soft preference multiplier for higher tiers (dedicated > hosted) and optional cost penalty for more expensive variants.
6) Composite score (lower is better):
   composite = w_p50 * smoothed_p50_norm + w_p95 * smoothed_p95_norm + w_net * (1 - net_health_score) + w_tier * tier_penalty + w_cost * cost_penalty
   suggested defaults: w_p50=0.2, w_p95=0.45, w_net=0.2, w_tier=0.1, w_cost=0.05

Decisioning and hysteresis:
- Soft thresholds: mark POPs as degraded if composite > degrade_threshold (e.g., 1.35) for long-window AND if short-window > spike_threshold (e.g., 1.8).
- Promote/demote with hysteresis: require sustained condition for promote/demote durations (promote after 2m stable, demote after 30s high short-window and 3m high long-window).
- Graceful switch: route a small fraction (1-5%) to candidate new POP for 30s before full shift. Use traffic shadowing and compare token cost/latency/error.

Variant escrow and fallback hierarchy:
- Maintain an escrowed list of compatible model variants (e.g., full, quantized, distilled) per route with compatibility metadata.
- Warm-up: when a variant is selected as fallback, start with canary traffic (0.5-2%) and run lightweight quality checks (BLEU-like or prompt-based evals) for 5-10 minutes.
- Auto-rollback: if quality metric delta > threshold OR error-rate increases, automatically revert and mark variant quarantined for 15m.

Observability and playground: 
- Expose composite_score, short/long EWMAs, net_health components, tier penalty, and weight breakdown per POP in Console.
- Add a per-route timeline view showing routing decisions, promotes/demotes, and variant transitions with links to the underlying telemetry windows.

Acceptance criteria:
- New scoring computed and stored once per 10s per POP for 95% of POPs in production.
- No more than 1 spurious full-POP switch per route per 24h attributable to telemetry noise in 90% of routes (measured in canary cohort).
- Variant fallback warmup prevents >80% of quality regressions compared to immediate fallback baseline.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit tests + offline replay using 30d telemetry -> run in dev cluster and validate composite score stability.
2) Canary: enable scoring for 5% of routes (low-traffic internal canary) with decisioning disabled (score-only).
3) Decisioning enabled for canary cohort with soft-promote percent=2%. Monitor for 72h.
4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with health gates.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Weight tuning: route-specific weight calibration vs global defaults. Proposal: start global, collect signals, adjust per-high-traffic routes via Console overrides.
- Storage: store EWMAs in existing metrics DB (prometheus) or a lightweight key-value store (Redis) for fast reads in route path? Preference: Redis cluster per region for read-latency.
- Complexity vs explainability: more signals improve accuracy but make Console explanations longer. Use breakdown UI and a simple "why" sentence.

Implementation notes:
- New service: routing-scorer (Go/Rust) reads telemetry from metrics bus, writes scores to Redis and emits metrics.
- Router changes: query Redis for top-N POPs per route and apply promote/demote logic locally with configured hysteresis.
- Variant orchestrator: extend existing variant manager with escrow state and canary toggles (feature flag driven).
comments: 2026-02-12 - Ava M: Triage meeting notes attached. Decided to prioritize stability over aggressive cost routing for Q1. Action: design EWMAs and thresholds.
2026-02-20 - Daniel K: Prototype EWMA windows implemented. Ran replay on 30 days of telemetry; composite score reduced flapping by ~37% in replay compared to naive p95-based selector.

2026-02-26 - Lina (PM): Design review feedback: expose user-facing sliders in Console for tier bias and short/long sensitivity. Also requested an opt-out per-customer flag for strict regional affinity.
2026-03-01 - SRE (Ravi): Raised concern about Redis cross-region failover during region outage. Suggested adding local fallback to read stale scores from Prometheus-derived cache.
2026-03-05 - Daniel K: Implemented canary warmup hooks in variant manager. Added integration tests for auto-rollback on quality delta.
2026-03-08 - QA: Running canary for 48h on internal routes. Early metrics look good; two routes flagged for manual weight tuning.
